🏦 Husband May Have to Pay Tax on Wife's FD, Gold & Share Income! 💰⚠️

Many taxpayers believe gifting money to a spouse can reduce taxes. However, under the "clubbing of income" provisions, income earned from assets gifted to a spouse may still be taxed in the hands of the person who made the gift.

💰 "FD Interest"
If a husband gifts money to his wife and she invests it in an FD, the "interest earned is generally taxable in the husband's hands".
📈 "Shares, Mutual Funds & Gold"
If the gifted money is invested in shares, mutual funds, gold, bonds, or similar assets, the "dividend, interest, and capital gains" are also generally clubbed with the husband's income.
🔄 "Reinvestment Exception"
Only the "first level of income" is clubbed. Any income earned from reinvesting that income is taxable in the wife's hands.

❌ "When Clubbing Doesn't Apply"
* Transfer for adequate consideration.
* Transfer before marriage.
* Transfer under a divorce or separation agreement.
* Investment made from the wife's own income, such as salary, business income, or inheritance.

⚠️ "Before gifting money for investments, understand the clubbing rules to avoid unexpected tax liability."
